content.text:
I fixed what I believe is the root cause, in `ScanStructure::ApplyResidualPredicate` (`src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp`). I couldn't build or run anything, so the fix is untested and I didn't run your repro.

The function first compacted `match_sel` in place down to the rows that passed the residual predicate. Only after that did it build the no-match list, by reading `match_sel` at the rows that failed. By then those slots had already been overwritten, so the no-match list held wrong row indices.

For SEMI/ANTI joins, `AdvancePointers` uses that list to keep walking the duplicate-key chain. With wrong indices, some probe rows were never checked against later chain entries. In your repro, `l(1,1)` matches `r(1,5)` on the key but fails the residual `1+5 > 2`... wait, it passes that check (6 > 2), and `r(1,1)` fails it (2 > 2 is false). Depending on chain order, the failed row could corrupt the list and the chain walk would stop early or follow the wrong rows. The result was wrong `found_match` flags, so `(1,1)` wrongly survived the ANTI join.

The fix moves the no-match collection to before the in-place compaction, so it reads the original `match_sel`. The compaction itself is safe, because it writes at an index that is never greater than the one it reads.
